stage-black.purpose: Rail, top bar, phone tab bar, Play bar, toast.

stage-raised.purpose: Hover fill on stage controls; Simple / Advanced track.

stage-ink.purpose: Text on the stage; Export pill fill.

stage-mute.purpose: Unselected nav, nav descriptions, Play bar labels.

spike-yellow.purpose: Position and Play: the torn you-are-here strip, Play button, selected genre, lit diagram notes (hit token). Never text on the light sheet.

accent.purpose: Controls: primary buttons, selected moods, outlines, focus. Deliberately equals ink.

play-green.purpose: The 7px playing stripe; bass note on keyboard diagrams.

tape-chromatic.purpose: Chromatic chords; same value as spike yellow.

sheet.purpose: Chart sheet, field fills, inset groups, torn-edge cut-out.

rule.purpose: Pane dividers, section rules, tab tracks.

chord-detail.purpose: The selected chord in the Chord panel.

chord-strip.purpose: Chord name on a tape strip, sized by container query; same face for Play bar now-playing (28px) and swap ideas (30px).

nav.purpose: Rail / tab-bar items, uppercase; 21px tablet, 19px phone. Play label 900 24px; brand 900 30px.

section.purpose: Verse / Chorus labels on the sheet, followed by a 2px rule.

body.purpose: Running text and hints, tabular figures.

control.purpose: Buttons, chips, segmented options; primary 700, small 13.5px.

mono.purpose: Text chart editor, fret numbers, voicing notes.

narrative.overview:
The song is laid out like a setlist taped to the stage floor. A stage-black rail and a stage-black Play bar frame a white sheet; on that sheet the chords sit on a beat grid as flat strips of gaffer tape, each strip coloured by its harmonic job and finished with one torn end. Spike yellow, the tape a stage crew uses to mark positions, marks where you are: the current screen in the navigation, the Play button, a picked genre, the notes lit on a guitar or piano diagram. Everything is glanceable from a stool with an instrument in your lap.

Hierarchy comes from scale contrast alone. Chord names and headings are set in Big Shoulders Display, condensed and heavy, uppercase for headings and huge for chords; everything around them is small, quiet Public Sans. A chord's name uses the same lettering everywhere it appears: on its strip, in the Chord panel, in swap ideas and in the Play bar. The surface is flat: tape lies on paper, the paper lies on the stage, and only things that really float above the stage (menus, the chord picker, a dragged strip, the toast) cast a shadow.

There is one shell for every view. The chart stays in the centre; a single navigation (Create, Chord, Tools) picks what the side panel shows, and Simple and Advanced share the same frame, with Simple hiding depth rather than rearranging the room. Light and dark themes both keep the stage black and the tape colours constant; only the sheet and the ink swap.
keyCharacteristics: Stage-black rail and Play bar framing a white (or charcoal) sheet.
Chords as flat 2px-cornered tape strips coloured by harmonic function, each with one torn right edge.
Spike yellow marks "you are here" and the Play action; a torn, slightly crooked strip of it sits behind the current nav item.
Controls are ink, never colour: the accent is ink, and colour is reserved for harmonic meaning and position.
Big Shoulders Display for chord names and headings, Public Sans for the interface, hierarchy by scale alone.
One mark per state on a chord: outline, green stripe, dashed edge, open frame, fade, lock.

rules.name: The Harmonic Job Rule
rules.body: Tape colour states a chord's function and nothing else. A tape colour never decorates a control, a heading or a panel.

rules.name: The Ink Controls Rule
rules.body: Controls speak in ink. The accent is ink, so a primary button, a selected chip and a selection outline are black on light and near-white on dark; colour is left free to mean harmony.

rules.name: The Spike Rule
rules.body: Spike yellow marks position and the go action: the current screen, Play, a picked style, the notes lit on a diagram. It is a fill with ink on it, or a mark on stage black; never body text on the light sheet.

rules.name: The One Lettering Rule
rules.body: A chord's name is Big Shoulders Display at 900 on its strip, in the Chord panel, in swap ideas and in the Play bar, so the chord you hear, see and swap reads as one object. New places that name a single chord follow the same lettering.

rules.name: The Scale Alone Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size and the display face, not from colour or boxes. Interface text stays small and quiet so the chords can be huge.

rules.name: The Raised Accidental Rule
rules.body: In Big Shoulders chord names, ♭ and ♯ stay in the text (so copy, search and screen readers get the real characters) but are painted transparent and overlaid with a raised b or # drawn in the chord face at 0.68em, 0.4em wide (0.46em for #).

rules.name: The Chart Never Leaves Rule
rules.body: Changing what the side panel shows never moves or hides the chart on desktop and tablet; on a phone the chart is its own tab, one tap away.

rules.name: The Floor Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Anything taped down (strips, chips, buttons, panels) lies flat. Only menus, the picker, a dragged strip and the toast lift.

rules.name: The Tape Or Key Rule
rules.body: If it represents a chord or a harmonic function, it is tape (2px corners, flat fill). If you press it, it is a key (pill). The function tag beside a chord name is tape too.

dos: **Do** colour a chord strip only by its harmonic function (tape-in-key, tape-borrowed, tape-secondary, tape-chromatic, tape-approach), with stage-black text on every tape colour in both themes.
**Do** keep the rail, top bar, phone tab bar, Play bar and toast stage black in both themes.
**Do** mark the current screen with the torn spike-yellow strip, rotated -1.1deg, behind the nav label.
**Do** set every chord name in Big Shoulders Display 900, with ♭ and ♯ drawn through the raised overlay.
**Do** make every control a pill with a 1.5px border, and every chord or function mark a 2px-cornered tape patch.

**Do** give each chord state exactly one mark: 3px ink outline (selected), 7px green bottom stripe (playing), dashed edge (outside Chords allowed), solid open frame with "?" (empty), 40% fade (tie), lock icon (locked).
**Do** draw new icons on the 16-unit grid at stroke 1.75, round caps and joins, in currentColor.
**Do** keep a new view inside the one shell: a side-panel choice in the single navigation, never a new layout.
donts: **Don't** use a tape colour on a button, heading, panel or chart decoration.
**Don't** set spike yellow (or the yellow tape colour) as text on the light sheet; it is a fill under ink, or a mark on stage black.
**Don't** put a shadow on a strip, chip, button or panel; only menus, the chord picker, a dragged strip and the toast float.
**Don't** round the tape: strips and function tags keep 2px corners and the torn right edge.
**Don't** add a second state mark to a strip (no glow plus outline, no colour change for selection).
**Don't** give Simple view its own layout; it hides depth inside the same shell.
